specificConditions: **Polarization Effect:** Dielectric material polarizes under an external field, creating an internal opposing field $E' = E_0 - E_{induced}$, which reduces the net electric field to $E = E_0/K$.
**Capacitance Enhancement:** Because $V = Ed$ decreases for a given charge Q when a dielectric is inserted ($V' = V/K$), the capacitance $C = Q/V'$ increases by a factor of K ($C' = KC_0$).

**Boundary Conditions:** At the interface of dielectric and free space, the normal component of electric displacement D ($D = \epsilon_0 E + P$) is continuous, while the tangential component of the electric field E is continuous.
